lore_anchors.definition: The floating jade palace in the sky, a central dungeon of this arc; locked translation for this major location.
A rare spirit beast capable of suppressing evil spirits; locked translation for this beast.
A powerful ghost type with horns and sharp claws, roughly equal to a late Foundation Establishment cultivator.
A rare zombie variant with green fur that can move in daylight; wields a bone fork that shoots ghost-fire.
A one-time seal of an animal or ghost soul into a magical treasure to boost its power; the seal can only be attempted once in the treasure’s lifespan.
A dark yin-attributed treasure refined for centuries, capable of emitting soul-binding yin qi and housing an artifact spirit.
Han Li’s signature flying sword; despite lacking an artifact spirit, it is highly refined and resists yin qi contamination.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is an artifact spirit in RMJI?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a once-per-lifetime seal: a cultivator may bind the soul of a beast or ghost into their magical treasure. The treasure gains a solid form and the spirit’s original abilities. If the seal fails, the treasure can never receive another spirit.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't Han Li put an artifact spirit into his flying swords?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has been hunting a true flood dragon for that purpose, but never found one in the Chaotic Star Sea. Without a suitable spirit, he has not yet performed the seal.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the ancient mirror shatter after saving Extreme Yin?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The mirror’s spiritual energy was consumed to repel the gray shadow’s attack, causing it to self-destruct. This is a common trope in xianxia: a one-use protective artifact.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Are artifact spirits common in RMJI?
cultural_notes_faq.a: No. Most cultivators either fail their seal attempt or never find a worthy spirit. The success rate is low, and the cost is high, so most treasures remain spiritless.
